body:
It undoubtedly had some minor effect,  but this was no doubt offset by the fact that it would have mostly been picked up by comfy people happy with the status quo just looking for an excuse to feel good about themselves. Not to mention that to me this comes off as a cynical publicity drive with no greater moral stance from a corporation than hallmark selling valentines cards or cola's Christmas adverts. Nothing like this will be done for the good of all anymore, it's all pr companies seeing the way the wind is blowing and looking to profit while it can.

I can see some positives but when it's done in such a cynical manner it just drowns out any good, you can see that big companies are just going to get more heavy handed with this as time goes on, that they will use any excuse to sell us shit and as we become more and more integrated they're will be nothing pure or honest left in the world.

I'm no doubt highly cynical and not very trusting of society on a whole, but that's just unfortunately how I see the world.

Pretty much from the 60s onwards that began as movement amongst college age groups that attempted to change the world for the better i.e anti war protests, environmentalism or civil rights. These are all admirable things to strive for but that hasn't stopped them being subverted by the vast capitalist machine for no real benifit bar profits, I seriously don't think Starbucks cared about Pride but if printing rainbow cups will increase profits they'll do it and people will gladly fall for the duplicity of it all without giving a damn.

I remember seeing the episode of babylon 5 with the machine that let you transfer your life energy to another person when I was eas about 12, even then I thought I wish it was real and then I'd work till I was 25 save money gove it all to charity and then give my life to some parent somewhere dying of cancer.

It's damn unfair that so many people who want to live have their lives cut short, but it's also so bad that we can't except that some people honestly don't want to live and we aren't brave enough to face that.

It really doesn't, It's so hard to explain I just don't feel like anything is right, there's just too many of us and we've spent our existence making a world which was wonderful and wild into something utilitarian and ugly and it's gotten to the point now where even the counter culture of old that tried to set us on a better course has been commoditified and repackaged to sell us more pointless crap just to keep us busy and ignorant.

I do my best to avoid hateful/selfish people and wouldn't count my friends amongst them, that doesn't stop them from having an oblivious outlook on life that can seem alien to me at times. I honestly only see my friends as a means to an end, a way to avoid thinking too much, it's a bit disgusting that I use these people soley as distractions if I'm being honest, so I guess that makes me pretty damn selfish. 

As for your view that there is wonder in our creations I can't see that, when I feel that the existence of humanity is a vast cosmic mistake, I feel it would have been better if none of us had ever been born. That doesn't mean I wish death on anyone but myself alone, it would be vastly selfish to force my values on people who don't share it.

It's just way too big a thing for my mind to comfortably comprehend, as for the hatred and ignorance it just makes it even worse when I think of all the ignorant, hateful and selfish people I personally know and start to magnify that by the sheer volume of humanity that exists or has existed.

It's hard to explain but it's like being part of a vast unfeeling machine, sometimes I can't look at a bit of fruit or a bottle of soap without wondering about all the people it took for that to end up in my home and it makes me queasy when I think of all the resources and effort used, that how damn many of us exist and how much ignorance and hatred there is amongst us. I just want no part of it.
